title: Eviction emulator and invariant checks for shard-local KV cache (LRU+TTL+prefix semantics)
creator: Riley Thompson
description: Build a deterministic eviction emulator and property-based invariant checker for the shard-local KV cache used by the serving runtime. The goal is to evaluate and validate combined eviction strategies (LRU, TTL, and prefix-aware pinning) under realistic continuous-batching traffic patterns and GPU memory constraints, and to produce concrete correctness guarantees we can assert in CI and at runtime. This work feeds into memory optimization efforts and prevents regressions that could cause incorrect model outputs or request failures when prefixes are evicted under load.
goals: Create a configurable simulator/emulator that replays request traces and models shard-local KV cache state transitions
Formalize a small set of invariants that capture correctness: prefix atomicity, no stale-kv leakage, eviction monotonicity, and memory bound guarantee
Implement property-based tests (fuzz traces) and deterministic unit tests against the invariants
Measure GPU memory savings and tail-latency impact under typical and pathological workloads
Ship invariant checks into CI and add runtime telemetry to surface violations
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can reproduce historical incident trace ID: inc-2025-11-kv-thrash (best-effort) and explain observed evictions
All property-based tests pass in CI (seeded fuzz corpus) for 1000 randomized traces
Integration tests show no correctness regressions when hybrid LRU+TTL+prefix pinning is enabled
Perf run shows >=10% GPU memory reduction on multi-tenant small-model workload without tail-latency increase > 5%
Telemetry emits a clear invariant-violation event with contextual keys when a runtime eviction would break prefix atomicity

design_decisions: Hybrid LRU+TTL: keep LRU for recency, use TTL as soft expiration to bound long-tail memory growth
Prefix pinning: track active prefix refcounts per shard and mark pinned entries as non-evictable until refcount reaches zero
Soft-reserve: introduce a small per-shard soft-reserve to prevent thrashing when many short-lived prefixes arrive
Deterministic eviction ordering in emulator: tie-breaker by insertion timestamp to allow reproducible replays
Runtime checks: only enable prefix-atomicity enforcement in canary mode initially; emit invariant violation events (non-fatal)
tradeoffs: LRU gives good recency but can thrash with many simultaneous prefixes; adding TTL helps but may prematurely evict hot keys
Pinning protects in-flight prefix consistency at the cost of temporarily increasing memory pressure; soft-reserve mitigates this but adds complexity
Strict atomicity enforcement could cause higher OOM protection actions (fallback to smaller models); therefore we'll start with observability-first approach
Emulator increases maintenance burden but allows us to reason about corner-cases that are hard to hit in perf labs
